levels.title: Hello, Fox
levels.instructions: Chapter 1: Orders. Grep Fox, this is Sudo Snake. Each floor panel is 100 steps wide, and the chip is 2 panels ahead. Type `step(200)` and press Run.

levels.title: Way Out
levels.instructions: A chip only counts once you get out with it. After the chip, keep walking until you stand on the green EXIT pad. One `step` can go as far as you like.
levels.starterCode: step(200)

levels.title: Corner
levels.instructions: The hall bends. `turn(-90)` turns Grep Fox to the left and `turn(90)` turns to the right. Walk to the corner, turn left, then head for the exit.
levels.starterCode: step(300)

levels.title: Two Chips
levels.instructions: Orders run from top to bottom, one at a time. Plan the whole route before you run it: chip, corner, corner, chip, exit.
levels.starterCode:
step(200)
turn(-90)

levels.title: About Face
levels.instructions: The chip is at the end of a dead-end hall and the exit is behind you. `turn(180)` turns Grep Fox all the way around.
levels.starterCode: step(250)

levels.title: Red Keycard
levels.instructions: A red door blocks the hall. A keycard opens every door of its color, so pick up the red keycard behind you first. The order of your orders matters.
levels.starterCode: step(400)

levels.title: Bad Intel
levels.instructions: HQ wrote these orders from old blueprints, and one number is wrong. Run them, watch where Grep Fox goes wrong, and fix only that line. Hover over a chip to see its x and y.
levels.starterCode:
step(200)
turn(-90)
step(200)
turn(90)
step(300)

levels.title: Locked Out
levels.instructions: Every order here is right, but one is in the wrong place: Grep Fox walks into the blue door before picking up the blue keycard. Move one line so the keycard comes first.
levels.starterCode:
step(150)
step(470)
turn(-90)
step(150)
turn(180)
step(150)
turn(-90)

levels.title: Wrong Way
levels.instructions: Someone mixed up left and right, so some turns go the wrong way. `turn(90)` turns right and `turn(-90)` turns left, as Grep Fox sees it. Find the bad turns and fix them.
levels.starterCode:
step(200)
turn(90)
step(150)
turn(90)
step(200)
turn(90)
step(150)
turn(90)
step(200)

levels.title: Boss: Gatehouse
levels.instructions: Boss fight. Two doors, two keycards, two chips and an exit. Plan every turn before you run. The gold diamond is bonus intel: it's optional, but HQ would love it.
levels.starterCode: step(300)

levels.title: Patrol Loop
levels.instructions: Chapter 2: Loops. A patrol around a square is the same two orders, four times. `for i in range(4):` repeats every line indented under it. Add a `turn(90)` inside the loop.
levels.starterCode:
for i in range(4):
    step(200)

levels.title: Service Stairs
levels.instructions: A loop can repeat several lines. One stair is: step 80, turn left, step 60, turn right. Put the whole stair inside the loop.

levels.title: Wrap It
levels.instructions: One tooth of this comb is already written. Put `for i in range(...):` above it, indent the six lines by 4 spaces, and count how many teeth there are.
levels.starterCode:
step(100)
turn(-90)
step(230)
turn(180)
step(230)
turn(-90)

levels.title: Indent Error
levels.instructions: Sudo Snake wrote this loop in a hurry. Only the lines indented under `for` repeat, and `turn(60)` slipped out. Fix the indentation. A hexagon has 6 corners of 60 degrees.

levels.title: Before and After
levels.instructions: Code above a loop runs once before it, and code below it (not indented) runs once after. Walk 100 out of the room first, take the four stairs down, then walk 150 to the exit.
levels.starterCode:
for i in range(4):
    turn(90)
    step(80)
    turn(-90)
    step(100)

levels.title: Up and Over
levels.instructions: A mountain of crates: three stairs up, then three stairs down to the exit. You can write two loops one after the other. The second loop starts back at the left edge, with no indent.
levels.starterCode:
for i in range(3):
    step(80)
    turn(-90)
    step(80)
    turn(90)

levels.title: Star Route
levels.instructions: A five-point star. Every turn is the same, and over the whole star Grep Fox spins around twice, so each turn is `2 * 360 / 5`. Python can work that out for you: write it straight inside `turn(...)`.

levels.title: Hurdles
levels.instructions: Three crates in a row, all the same size, with a chip behind each one. Write how to get over one crate (up 110, right 140, down 110, right 60), then repeat it 3 times. Stay under the laser.

levels.title: Off by One
levels.instructions: This octagon patrol stops one side short of the exit. `range(1, 8)` counts 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7: only 7 numbers. Fix the loop so it runs 8 times.

levels.title: Boss: Factory Floor
levels.instructions: Boss fight. Hop the three crates with a loop, then head up to the blue keycard and out through the blue door to the exit. Code after the loop runs once.

levels.title: Name It
levels.instructions: Chapter 3: Variables. A variable is a name for a value: `side = 150` stores 150 under the name `side`. The vault is 150 wide. Store it once, then use `side` instead of the number everywhere it's needed.
levels.starterCode:
side = 100
step(100)
turn(90)
step(100)
turn(90)
step(100)
turn(90)
step(100)

levels.title: HQ Feed
levels.instructions: The building changes every night, and this mission checks your code in 3 versions of the room. HQ sends the vault size as `size` (top right of the map). Use `size`, not a number, so one program works in every room.

levels.title: Stair Feed
levels.instructions: Every night the stairs are rebuilt. HQ sends the size of one stair as `run` (along) and `rise` (up). There are always 4 stairs.
levels.starterCode:
for i in range(4):
    step(80)
    turn(-90)
    step(60)
    turn(90)

levels.title: Count Feed
levels.instructions: The comb grows and shrinks each night. HQ counts the teeth for you in `teeth`. A loop can repeat a variable number of times: `range(teeth)`.
levels.starterCode:
for i in range(4):
    step(100)
    turn(-90)
    step(230)
    turn(180)
    step(230)
    turn(-90)

levels.title: Growing Spiral
levels.instructions: Each side is 40 steps longer than the one before. A variable can change: `side = side + 40` takes the old value, adds 40 and stores the result back under the same name. Put that inside the loop.
levels.starterCode:
side = 40
for i in range(7):
    step(side)
    turn(90)

levels.title: Shrinking Spiral
levels.instructions: The loop variable can be the distance itself. Run this code: `print(side)` shows each value under your code. Then make Grep Fox step that far and turn right each time round.
levels.starterCode:
for side in range(300, 0, -60):
    print(side)

levels.title: Lost Value
levels.instructions: These stairs get bigger each time, but Grep Fox keeps taking the same small steps. One line works out the new gap and then throws the answer away. Fix that line so the result is stored.
levels.starterCode:
gap = 60
for i in range(4):
    step(gap)
    turn(-90)
    step(gap)
    turn(90)
    gap + 20

levels.title: Two Feeds
levels.instructions: Now the vault is a rectangle, and HQ sends both `width` and `height`. Going around a rectangle means: width, turn, height, turn, and then the same again.

levels.title: Halfway
levels.instructions: A chip waits at the end of each arm of this cross, `size / 2` from the middle. Go out and back four times, then end in the middle on the exit. Store `size / 2` in a variable called `half` so you only work it out once.
levels.starterCode: half = 100

levels.title: Boss: Night Shift
levels.instructions: Boss fight. Climb `floors` stairs, each 80 along and `rise` up. Then go straight up to the top hall (it is at y = 80, so the climb is `360 - floors * rise`), pick up the red keycard, and go left through the red door to the exit.
levels.starterCode:
for i in range(floors):
    step(80)

levels.title: Rooms in a Row
levels.instructions: Chapter 4: Loops in loops. Three rooms, each a square of 100. Walking around one room is a loop. Put that loop inside another loop that does it 3 times, with a `step(200)` to the next room after each lap.

levels.title: Flower
levels.instructions: One square petal is written. Put a loop around it that makes 6 petals, with `turn(60)` after each one. The inner loop runs all the way through every time the outer loop goes round once.

levels.title: Nested Vaults
levels.instructions: Five vaults share one corner, each 50 bigger than the last. The inner loop can use the outer loop's variable: walk the 4 sides of a vault with `step(size * 50)`.
levels.starterCode:
for size in range(1, 6):
    print(size * 50)

levels.title: Which Loop?
levels.instructions: Indentation decides which loop a line belongs to. `step(160)` should happen once per room, not once per side. Move it so it belongs to the outer loop.

levels.title: Bar Chart
levels.instructions: Bar number `col` is `col` levels tall, with a chip on every level. Climb one level at a time with an inner `for level in range(col):`, come back down, then move 100 to the right.
levels.starterCode:
for col in range(1, 6):
    turn(-90)
    # climb col levels
    turn(180)
    step(col * 60)
    turn(-90)
    step(100)

levels.title: Grid Feed
levels.instructions: HQ sends `rows` and `cols`. Walk along a row collecting a chip every 80 steps, walk back, drop 80 down to the next row and turn to face right again. Rows outside, columns inside.
levels.starterCode:
for c in range(cols):
    step(80)

levels.title: Garden Corners
levels.instructions: A spiral with a little 40-step room at each corner. Each lap of the spiral walks `i * 70`, sweeps the room with an inner loop (step 40, turn left, 4 times), then turns right.

levels.title: Mixed-up Names
levels.instructions: These vaults should grow, but every side is the wrong length, and the first one is 0. The inner loop uses the wrong loop variable. Which name holds the vault number?

levels.title: Tents
levels.instructions: Four triangle tents in a row. A triangle has 3 sides and you turn 120 degrees at each corner: use `turn(-120)` to go up and over. After each tent, `step(160)` to the next one.

levels.title: Boss: Warehouse
levels.instructions: Boss fight. Circle each rack (a square of `size`, going up with `turn(-90)`), with `step(size + 40)` to reach the next. After the last rack the red keycard is right in front of you. Then go down through the red door to the exit, 140 below.

levels.title: Hop
levels.instructions: Chapter 5: Functions. A function gives a name to a group of orders: `def hop():` defines it and `hop()` runs it. The crates aren't evenly spaced, so a loop won't fit, but you can call `hop()` wherever you need it. Hop all three, then walk to the exit.
levels.starterCode:
def hop():
    turn(-90)
    step(80)
    turn(90)
    step(100)
    turn(90)
    step(80)
    turn(-90)

step(80)
hop()

levels.title: Detours
levels.instructions: Three crates on three different walls. Write `def around():` once (turn left, 70, turn right, 120, turn right, 70, turn left). The turns are relative to the way Grep Fox faces, so the same detour works on every wall.
levels.starterCode:
def around():
    turn(-90)
    step(70)
    # finish the detour

step(100)
around()

levels.title: Square Sizes
levels.instructions: Functions can take inputs. In `def square(size):` the name `size` holds whatever number you pass in, so `square(80)` and `square(160)` walk different squares. Sizes here: 80, 160, 120 and 200, with steps of 120, 200 and 160 between them.
levels.starterCode:
def square(size):
    # walk 4 sides of length size, turning left
    pass

square(80)

levels.title: Two Inputs
levels.instructions: A function can take more than one input: `def rect(w, h):`. Walk around three rectangles: `rect(200, 80)`, then `step(240)` and `rect(100, 240)`, then `step(140)` and `rect(150, 150)`.
levels.starterCode:
def rect(w, h):
    pass

levels.title: Too Soon
levels.instructions: Run this and read the error. Python reads your code from top to bottom, so a function has to be defined before the line that calls it. Move the `def` block to the top.
levels.starterCode:
for i in range(3):
    zigzag()

def zigzag():
    turn(-45)
    step(141)
    turn(90)
    step(141)
    turn(-45)

levels.title: Flights
levels.instructions: A function can call another function. `stair()` climbs one stair. Write `flight(n)` to climb `n` stairs with a loop, then climb flights of 3, 2 and 4 with a `step(80)` landing between them.
levels.starterCode:
def stair():
    step(50)
    turn(-90)
    step(40)
    turn(90)

def flight(n):
    pass

levels.title: Branches
levels.instructions: Each branch off the hall has a chip at its end, and every branch is a different length. Write `branch(length)`: turn left, go in, turn around, come back, turn left. Branches are 150, 250 and 90 long and 150 apart, starting 100 ahead.
levels.starterCode:
def branch(length):
    pass

step(100)
branch(150)

levels.title: Mixed Signals
levels.instructions: `rect(w, h)` takes the width first and the height second, but the call gives them the other way round, so Grep Fox runs into the laser. Inputs are matched by position. Fix the call.
levels.starterCode:
def rect(w, h):
    for i in range(2):
        step(w)
        turn(-90)
        step(h)
        turn(-90)

rect(120, 320)

levels.title: Function Feed
levels.instructions: Two vaults, a small one and a big one, and their sizes change every night. HQ sends `small` and `big`. Write `vault(size)` once and call it with each. There is a gap of 60 between the vaults.

levels.title: Boss: Assembly Line
levels.instructions: Boss fight. Station `i` is a square of `i * 40`, and there are `stations` of them, 40 apart. Write `station(size)`, loop over the stations, then grab the blue keycard and go up through the blue door to the exit, 320 above. Beat this boss to unlock the drone.
levels.starterCode:
def station(size):
    pass

levels.title: Drone Launch
levels.instructions: Chapter 6: Objects. The drone is an object: `d = launch_drone()` stores it in `d`, and `d.step(400)` gives the order to the drone instead of Grep Fox. It flies over lasers. Fly it to the fuse box, `d.zap()` it, then walk Grep Fox to the chip.
levels.starterCode: d = launch_drone()

levels.title: Battery Budget
levels.instructions: The drone only has 300 battery, and every step uses some. Flying right and then up costs too much. Objects have methods that answer questions: `d.turn_to(fuses[0])` and `d.distance_to(fuses[0])` take the straight line. Use `print(d.battery)` to check what's left.
levels.starterCode:
d = launch_drone()
d.step(180)
d.turn(-90)
d.step(200)
d.zap()

levels.title: Chip List
levels.instructions: Lists. `chips` is a list of every chip in the room, and `for c in chips:` takes them one at a time. `turn_to(c)` faces a chip and `distance_to(c)` says how far away it is. The chips move every night, so let the list do the counting.
levels.starterCode: print(chips)

levels.title: Who Goes?
levels.instructions: Grep Fox is an object too: `fox`. Write `go(who, target)` so it works for any agent: `who.turn_to(target)`, then `who.step(who.distance_to(target))`. Send the drone to the fuse box and zap it, then send `fox` to every chip in the laser box.
levels.starterCode:
def go(who, target):
    who.turn_to(target)
    # move who all the way to target

d = launch_drone()
go(d, fuses[0])

levels.title: Backwards
levels.instructions: Tonight the list is in the worst order: `chips[0]` is behind the red door, and the red keycard sits on the last chip, `chips[-1]`. `reversed(chips)` goes through a list from the end to the start.

levels.title: Right Angles
levels.instructions: A searchlight sits on every straight line between chips. Go along the floor lines instead: first across to the corner `(c.x, fox.y)`, then up or down to the chip. Every object has `x` and `y`, and `(c.x, fox.y)` makes a new point from them.

levels.title: Fuse Chain
levels.instructions: Two laser fences, each wired to its own fuse box, and just enough battery to fly from one fuse box to the next. `fuses` is a list too: loop over it with the drone, zapping each one, then loop over `chips` with Grep Fox.
levels.starterCode: d = launch_drone()

levels.title: Wrong Agent
levels.instructions: One order went to the wrong agent: Grep Fox walks straight into the laser while the drone stays home. The name before the dot decides who obeys. Fix that one line.
levels.starterCode:
d = launch_drone()
step(300)
d.zap()
step(500)

levels.title: Waypoints
levels.instructions: You can make your own lists: `route = [(250, 100), (550, 100)]` is a list of points. Add the points that take Grep Fox over the crates and down to the last chip at `(700, 400)`, and the loop does the walking.
levels.starterCode:
route = [(250, 100)]
for p in route:
    turn_to(p)
    step(distance_to(p))

levels.title: Boss: Blackout
levels.instructions: Boss fight. The laser box is wired to two fuse boxes, and the drone has just enough battery for both. Write `go(who, target)`, zap every fuse with the drone, send Grep Fox to every chip, then to the `exit_pad`. Beat this boss to unlock the scanner.

levels.title: Decoys
levels.instructions: Chapter 7: Decisions. Some chips are decoys wired to the alarm, and they change every night. Every chip has `trapped`, which is `True` or `False`. `if not c.trapped:` runs the lines under it only for real chips.

levels.title: Short or Long
levels.instructions: Some nights the red keycard is on the floor ahead of you, and some nights it isn't. `has_key('red')` is `True` or `False`. Use `if` for the short way through the red door and `else` for the long way over the top (up 170, along 450, down 170).

levels.title: Fork
levels.instructions: You've unlocked the scanner: `ahead()` says how far Grep Fox can walk before hitting something. At the fork, one way is blocked tonight. Face left, and if `ahead()` is less than 60, turn around. Walk 300 to the end of the hall, then `turn_to(chips[0])` and step 100.
levels.starterCode:
step(200)
turn(-90)
print(ahead())

levels.title: Color Code
levels.instructions: Tonight's keycard could be red, blue or green, and each opens one hall: red at the top, blue in the middle, green at the bottom. `elif` checks another condition only if the ones above it were False, and `else` catches the rest.
levels.starterCode:
step(100)
if has_key('red'):
    turn(-90)
    step(150)
    turn(90)

levels.title: Equals
levels.instructions: Run this and read the error. In Python `=` stores a value and `==` compares two values. For `True` or `False` you can skip the comparison: `if c.trapped:` is enough.

levels.title: Turn at Walls
levels.instructions: A different maze every night, but each one only ever turns right. Repeat one simple rule: if `ahead()` is under 60, `turn(90)`, otherwise `step(100)`. A loop of 30 is plenty, because the mission ends as soon as the chip is yours.
levels.starterCode:
for i in range(30):
    step(100)

levels.title: Stray Line
levels.instructions: Grep Fox stops turning towards decoys, but still walks off for each one. Indentation decides what belongs to the `if`. Find the line that slipped out of the `if` block.

levels.title: Gatekeeper
levels.instructions: A laser fence splits the room, and the only gap is at the top, around `(400, 75)`. Before each chip, check: if the chip is on the right (`c.x > 400`) `and` Grep Fox is on the left (`fox.x < 400`), go through the gap first. Then the same check the other way.

levels.title: Maze Runner
levels.instructions: These mazes turn both ways. When the way ahead is blocked, try turning right, and if that's blocked too, turn all the way round to face left. An `if` inside an `if` lets you make the second check only when you need it.

levels.title: Boss: Checkpoint
levels.instructions: Boss fight. Skip the decoys, use the gap at the top of the laser fence to change sides, then go to `(560, 250)`. If the red keycard was there, go down to `(560, 420)` and through the red door to the exit. If not, go round through `(770, 300)` and `(770, 430)`.

levels.title: Until the Exit
levels.instructions: Chapter 8: While loops. `for` repeats a set number of times, but `while` repeats as long as something is true. The exit is a different distance away every night. Keep stepping 100 `while fox.x < exit_pad.x:`.
levels.starterCode:
while fox.x < exit_pad.x:
    print(fox.x)

levels.title: Unknown Hurdles
levels.instructions: Tonight there could be 1, 2 or 3 crates. `hop()` clears one crate and lands 200 further on. Hop `while` Grep Fox is still short of the exit, then take the last 60 steps.
levels.starterCode:
def hop():
    turn(-90)
    step(80)
    turn(90)
    step(100)
    turn(90)
    step(80)
    turn(-90)
    step(100)

hop()

levels.title: Maze and Out
levels.instructions: Use your maze rule, but this time don't stop when the chip is collected: then you still need to leave by the exit. Loop `while not chips[0].collected:`, then `turn_to(exit_pad)` and step 100.
levels.starterCode:
while not chips[0].collected:
    step(100)

levels.title: Blink
levels.instructions: This laser switches on and off, and the timing changes every night. Walk up to it (260 steps), wait `while lasers[0].on:` in small `wait(0.1)` steps, and cross as soon as it goes off.
levels.starterCode:
step(260)
wait(1)
step(290)

levels.title: Gauntlet
levels.instructions: Three blinking lasers, each with its own rhythm. A laser that's off right now might switch on while you're crossing, so wait for a fresh gap: wait `while laser.on`, and before that, wait `while not laser.on` so you catch the moment it switches off. Walk to 40 short of each laser (`laser.x - 40 - fox.x`), then cross with `step(80)`.
levels.starterCode:
for laser in lasers:
    step(laser.x - 40 - fox.x)

levels.title: Watch the Bug
levels.instructions: A Sentry Bug patrols up and down across your path, at a different speed every night. Your code can watch it: wait `while guards[0].y > 100:`, so you set off the moment it reaches the top. Then cross.
levels.starterCode:
step(150)
wait(2)
step(400)

levels.title: Counter
levels.instructions: Walk down the hall 100 at a time `while ahead() > 60:`, grab the chip at the end, then come all the way back to the exit where you started. A variable that goes up by 1 each time round, `count = count + 1`, remembers how far you went.

levels.title: Endless
levels.instructions: This loop never ends: nothing inside it changes `fox.x`, so the condition stays True forever and HQ stops the mission. Make Grep Fox move inside the loop.
levels.starterCode:
while fox.x < 600:
    wait(0.1)

levels.title: Two Bugs
levels.instructions: Two Sentry Bugs at different speeds. Wait `while guards[0].y > 100:` so you cross the first one's path as it reaches the top, wait at the chip between the crates, then do the same for `guards[1]`.
levels.starterCode:
while guards[0].y > 100:
    wait(0.1)

levels.title: Boss: Night Watch
levels.instructions: Boss fight. Along the bottom hall: grab the first chip, wait out the blinking laser, hop over the decoy (up 60, along 80, down 60), grab the next chip. Then wait for the Sentry Bug to reach the top of its patrol, and run for the exit. Beat this boss to unlock the hacking kit.

levels.title: First Hack
levels.instructions: Chapter 9: Problem solving. You have the hacking kit. Next to a terminal, `hack(answer)` sends an answer, and a wrong one sets off the alarm. Tonight's question: what is the total of `terminals[0].data`? Add it up with a loop: `total = total + n`.
levels.starterCode:
print(terminals[0].data)
total = 0

levels.title: Biggest
levels.instructions: The terminal wants the biggest number in its data. Start with `biggest = data[0]`, then go through the list: `if n > biggest:`, keep `n` instead.
levels.starterCode:
data = terminals[0].data
biggest = data[0]

levels.title: Count Them
levels.instructions: Question: how many numbers in the data are more than 50? Start a counter at 0 and add 1 each time `n > 50`.
levels.starterCode: count = 0

levels.title: Return
levels.instructions: Two terminals ask the same question: the total of their data. Write `total(numbers)` once. `return result` hands the answer back to whoever called it, so `hack(total(terminals[0].data))` works. The second terminal is 230 further on.
levels.starterCode:
def total(numbers):
    result = 0
    # add up the numbers
    return result

levels.title: Build a List
levels.instructions: Make a new list of only the real chips: start with `real = []` and `real.append(c)` for every chip that isn't trapped. The terminal asks how many there are: `len(real)`. Then go and collect them.
levels.starterCode: real = []

levels.title: Average
levels.instructions: The terminal wants the average of its data: the total divided by how many numbers there are. `len(data)` counts them, and `/` divides.
levels.starterCode: data = terminals[0].data

levels.title: Print or Return
levels.instructions: `biggest` shows the right number under your code, but the terminal still says ACCESS DENIED. `print` only shows a value; it doesn't hand it back. A function with no `return` gives back `None`.

levels.title: Nearest First
levels.instructions: The chips sit in a ring around a searchlight, and the list jumps across the ring, so going in list order walks straight into the light. Write `nearest()` to return the closest chip not yet collected, and always go to that one next.

levels.title: Sorted
levels.instructions: This terminal wants its data back in order, from smallest to largest. Python has a built-in function for that: `sorted(data)` returns a new, sorted list.
levels.starterCode:
data = terminals[0].data
print(data)

levels.title: Boss: Data Heist
levels.instructions: Boss fight. The terminal asks how many decoys are in the room. Then collect every real chip, always the nearest one next, so you go round the ring and not across the searchlight in the middle. Finish on the exit pad.

levels.title: Recon
levels.instructions: Chapter 10: Final operations. Everything you know, in one mission. Zap every fuse with the drone, collect only the real chips inside the laser box, and leave by the exit pad.

levels.title: Locksmith
levels.instructions: Each chip is locked in a cell behind a colored door, and the keycards are scattered around the room. Loop over `keys` to collect every keycard, then for each chip go to `(520, c.y)` in front of its door, walk in, and come back out the same way.

levels.title: Guard Rotation
levels.instructions: Two Sentry Bugs and a blinking laser. Write `wait_top(g)` that waits until a guard reaches the top, and `wait_gap(laser)` that waits for a fresh gap. Then: wait for bug 0, step 290 to the chip, wait for bug 1, step 290, wait for the gap, step 100.

levels.title: Code Breaker
levels.instructions: Two terminals, two questions. The first wants the biggest number in its data. The second, 230 further on, wants how many of its numbers are over 50. Write a function for each, with `return`.

levels.title: Spiral Vault
levels.instructions: A spiral of corner rooms that changes every night. HQ sends `first` (the first side), `grow` (how much longer each side gets) and `turns`. At each corner, sweep a 40 room with `turn(-90)`, then turn right and carry on.
levels.starterCode: side = first

levels.title: Scanner Sweep
levels.instructions: A maze with chips along the way and the exit at the far end. Follow your maze rule `while distance_to(exit_pad) > 30:`.
levels.starterCode:
while distance_to(exit_pad) > 30:
    pass

levels.title: Bug Hunt
levels.instructions: HQ's own code has three bugs in it. Run it, read what goes wrong, fix one bug, and run it again. Check the function's answer, who flies to the fuse box, and which chips get collected.

levels.title: Drone Escort
levels.instructions: Three laser fences, three fuse boxes and three chips, and both lists are in the same order. Go through them by number: for each `i`, the drone zaps `fuses[i]`, then Grep Fox collects `chips[i]`. The drone only has enough battery to hop from one fuse box to the next.

levels.title: Inventory
levels.instructions: The terminal wants the `x` of every real chip, as a list sorted from smallest to largest. Build the list with `append`, `hack(sorted(...))` it, then collect the real chips.
levels.starterCode: xs = []

levels.title: Boss: Grand Heist
levels.instructions: Final boss. Hack the terminal with the number of decoys. Send the drone to zap the laser fence. Wait at `(340, 250)` for the Sentry Bug to arrive at the top: if it's already up there it may be about to leave, so let it go first. Then cross to `(620, 250)`. Collect every real chip and get out. Good luck, Grep Fox.
